quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Turn only your head to look where you want to go. Keep your shoulders and eyes level.

questions.question: Which is a bad reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a person in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians who might move into your lane. Do not use it to get attention.

questions.question: In a group ride, newer riders should be positioned:

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Newer riders should ride right behind the leader. This prevents them from falling behind and lets experienced riders watch them.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of your lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Ride in the center of the lane at all times.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Move your position in the lane as needed. There is no single best position for all situations.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of your lane is safest when being passed. Riding on either side increases the risk of a collision.

questions.question: If you ride a three-wheeled motorcycle or have a sidecar, do not ride too far to the right because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will have trouble passing other vehicles.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is on the right side. Riding too far right can cause the sidecar or rear wheel to leave the road.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep proper space between riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and keep proper spacing. Check your mirrors regularly. Put experienced riders at the front and back to lead and watch the group.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply more pressure to the front brake.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply more pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply more pressure to the front brake.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward, the front wheel grips the road better. You can then apply more front brake pressure.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: As weight shifts to the front of your bike while braking, you should:

options.text: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
Do nothing. Weight transfer has no effect.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: Gradually apply more pressure to the front brake as the bike's weight moves forward.

questions.question: Who should set the pace in a group of riders?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider in back
questions.explanation: The last rider in a group should set the pace. This makes sure no riders are left behind.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down as much as possible before hitting it. Keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and ease off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for group riding. However, riders should switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from injury and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
Grab at the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply gradually increasing pressure for smooth, controlled braking.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol causes many motorcycle crashes, especially fatal ones. Research shows that about 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: When exiting a highway while riding in a group, which formation should be used?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to single-file when going through curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger in the vehicle may tell the driver that you are there.
Is illegal because you have to ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog. Then accelerate and leave it behind. If a larger animal is approaching, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following will help you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce speed and use both brakes. Avoid sudden movements. Stay away from the center lane and follow tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: A helmet should NOT:

options.text: Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no visible damage. A helmet used in a crash must be replaced because it may be damaged inside, even if it looks fine.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move far to the right to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on either side of the lane is risky. The side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. The far side may cause them to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay on the left side of your lane.
Stay in the middle of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.
Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind. Riding on the side nearest the passing driver increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause them to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane offer a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane provides three paths: the left side, center, and right side of the lane.
